data.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1191 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1191), based on
main ceea74366. Plan PASSED on round 4; the three earlier rounds each found something real and the
corrections are recorded below because two of them changed the design.

=== WHAT SHIPPED ===
`Backend` DECLARES `remote_ref()`. Both concrete backends implement it, returning a `RemoteRef`
whose `instance` comes from a new pure helper (`adapters/jira_family/deployment.py`,
`instance_from_base_url`) and is INJECTED AT CONSTRUCTION by the `build_backend` factories, which
already hold resolved settings. 14 held-out tests; both ADRs amended; `make lint` and
`make typecheck` clean; no file over the module-size cap.

=== THE CORRECTION THIS TICKET ACTUALLY DELIVERS ===
`RemoteRef`'s docstring claimed `instance` exists "so two instances of the same vendor never
collide". Verified in source rather than reasoned about, that ran two things together:
  * Cloud vs DC was ALREADY separated by `vendor` itself (`"jira"` vs `"jira-datacenter"`), so
    `instance` was never needed for that. What it disambiguates is two deployments of the SAME
    vendor.
  * `instance` does NOT prevent the collision that bites. The colliding value is the LOCAL TICKET
    ID, and `_jira_key_to_local_id` is `"jira-" + jira_key.lower()` — derived from the Jira key
    and nothing else. Two DC deployments each owning a project `DIG` both mint `jira-dig-123`
    whatever `instance` says, because nothing reads it at mint time.
Both ADRs are amended (`0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md`, `0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md`)
and a test pins the limitation, saying explicitly that IT is the test which should go red if the
id scheme is ever made deployment-aware — a breaking store-wide migration deliberately not done.

=== THREE PLAN-REVIEW ROUNDS, AND WHAT EACH FIXED ===
R1 BLOCKED (2 findings, one problem): "construct a RemoteRef on the inbound path" named no
RECEIVER, so the value would be a discarded local and the "assert on the object the pass built"
criterion was unsatisfiable. The codebase answered it: `backend_support.FakeBackend` has
implemented `remote_ref()` since J7 while the PORT never declared it and no real backend provided
one — the contract tests were running against a fake strictly MORE capable than production. That
asymmetry is the defect underneath this ticket, and the port member is the receiver.
R2 BLOCKED (3 findings): (a) my claim "bindings already key on the immutable numeric id per 7c26"
was WRONG — verified in `binding_store.py`, the primary key is still the Jira KEY
(`entry["jira_key"]`, `reverse[jira_key]`) and 7c26's `record_jira_id` is an ADDITIVE re-key
fallback. WITHDRAWN rather than repaired: the argument (nothing persists a `RemoteRef`) never
needed it. (b) `remote_ref()` as planned would resolve settings at CALL time, which breaks a
contract test constructed without config — corrected to constructor injection, citing cd78's
`Verified -1` (Python 3.12 changed runtime-checkable `Protocol` `isinstance` from `hasattr` to
`inspect.getattr_static`, so a settings-resolving property that raises breaks `isinstance` on CI's
3.11 while passing locally on 3.13).
R3 BLOCKED (2 findings): an AC tension between "no ambient config" and "non-empty instance" —
resolved by making the test pass the instance EXPLICITLY, which is what proves constructor-state
reading; and Scope naming no ADR file, when two carry the claim.
MY OWN LESSON-4 SWEEP then caught a leftover the reviewer had not: an AC still carried the
withdrawn 7c26 justification, and three passages still said "the ADR" singular after Scope changed
to "BOTH ADRs". Fixed before re-review. Grepping the whole document after an edit keeps paying.

=== THE TESTS, AND WHICH HALF MATTERS ===
For the helper, the load-bearing half is that equivalent SPELLINGS AGREE — trailing slash, host
case, default port, scheme, omitted scheme — because a helper that merely echoed its input would
pass "different deployments differ" trivially. Distinctness is checked on the two cases a naive
host-only implementation would merge: a shared host differing only by CONTEXT PATH (DC is commonly
served at `/jira`) and a NON-default port.
For the port member: both REAL backends are constructed with an explicit instance and NO ambient
config, and a second construction WITHOUT the argument must return the empty default — which is
what distinguishes "used what it was given" from "found a value elsewhere".

=== NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY ===
No consumer is wired into any pass: nothing reads a `RemoteRef` today, and threading a call through
a path that does not use it would be ceremony that reads as coverage. The port member is the
deliverable; a consumer arrives with the story that needs one. No new config key. No change to
`_jira_key_to_local_id`.
